    Settings & help

    How to update

    Google live traffic opens Google’s current traffic view. Reload that Google Maps view to request traffic again.

    To update your comparison: open a station, check its red stretch against the map scale, then use Add your check. It saves on this device.

    To update the map for everyone, the owner can publish a shared observation ↗: choose Run workflow, select the station, enter the length, actual Bali observation time and a short note. GitHub validates, saves and publishes it.

    Reload saved data ↻ fetches those published measurements. It does not remeasure Google traffic. This site has no automatic traffic feed.

    How the comparison works

    Lengths are approximate measurements of red/dark-red stretches against Google Maps’ scale. Each station shows its actual observation time. The initial observations are from 14 October 2026, around 10:45 WITA.

    A red stretch ending at a station, with green beyond, can indicate a fuel queue. Junctions, through traffic and separate pump lines also affect it. The pin colours compare recorded lengths; this map does not receive a live Google traffic feed.

    Open Google live traffic to check conditions now. Recorded lengths are a starting comparison, not confirmation that petrol is available.

    Observations more than one hour old are marked as older. Reload fetches the latest saved dataset; it does not remeasure Google’s traffic.

    Your checks and privacy

    Use Add your check on a station to record what you see. These checks and your selected starting point stay in this browser. They are not sent to other visitors. A newer published observation takes priority over an older personal check. Checks saved on the original Sites address do not transfer to this address.

    Your location is requested only when you press “Use my location”. Directions open Google Maps with the starting point you selected.

    Distances and waiting estimates

    Distances are straight-line distances from your selected starting point. Driving routes can be longer.

    The optional waiting calculator assumes that the entire entered red stretch is a motorbike queue. It estimates bikes ahead from spacing and rows, then divides by the combined service rate of the active pumps. All inputs are adjustable. It excludes any queue inside the station and cannot account for an empty tank at the station or a stopped pump.

    Coverage and sources

    Five mapped stations around Nusa Dua and Jimbaran. Unchecked stations are left unranked. Fuel availability is unknown until someone records a check; every report can become outdated.

    Station names, coordinates and traffic observations: Google Maps. Basemap: OpenFreeMap / OpenStreetMap. This is an independent comparison tool.
